chunks: From him, from Fadalah, from Rifah ibn Musa, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked while I was present about the sale of fresh fruit juice (asir) from those who ferment it, so he said: 'It is permissible. Do we not sell our dates to someone who turns them into a bad/drunken drink?'

key_terms.ٱلْعَصِيرِ: Fresh fruit juice, specifically grape juice, before fermentation

ai.seo_question: Is fresh fruit juice (asir) considered halal if it ferments into wine?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the principle of *taba' al-asl* (the subsidiary follows the principal), ruling that fresh juice (*asir*) remains halal when sold to those who ferment it into wine, as the intrinsic nature of the fruit does not change. This ruling is often cited by Shia jurists to distinguish between the permissibility of the substance itself and the permissibility of its consumption in a specific state, emphasizing that the buyer's intent or subsequent use does not render the original commodity impure.
